name: deeper-head
hypothesis: Dense(128, relu) hidden layer before output learns nonlinear combinations of YAMNet embeddings, improving buzz sensitivity

baseline.note: different dataset (standard vs lite) — not a clean comparison

conclusion: MLP head worse than linear probe; confounded by lite vs standard set — see deeper-std for clean comparison

name: deeper-std
hypothesis: Adding Dense(128, relu) before output improves over linear probe when trained on standard (not lite) set
conclusion: MLP head is worse than linear probe at high-precision operating point on standard set; linear probing outperforms on YAMNet embeddings

name: combined-embedder
hypothesis: Validate on all classes instead of buzz-only so early stopping calibrates against full precision/recall distribution
conclusion: Marginal improvement at high-precision point (+0.4pp at 95% precision); principled default but not a major lever

name: focal-loss
hypothesis: Focal loss (gamma=2, alpha=0.25) improves sensitivity at 95% precision by downweighting easy negatives
conclusion: Primary metric essentially unchanged; alpha=0.25 penalizes buzz too aggressively — retry with alpha=0.5–0.75

name: focal-loss-alpha
hypothesis: Focal loss with alpha=0.75 corrects over-penalization of buzz in alpha=0.25 experiment
conclusion: Focal loss shifts operating point rather than lifting PR curve; dead end for 95% precision metric

name: label-smooth
hypothesis: Label smoothing (eps=0.1) improves score calibration, lifting sensitivity at 95% precision
conclusion: Best result so far: +2.2pp at 95% precision (0.2763 vs 0.2545); 0.4pp below production target (0.28); try eps=0.05 or LR reduction to close gap
